place.source_title: Morgan Park Historic District, Eighty-seventh Avenue

brief: US Steel company-town houses of Morgan Park (built from c.1913 in cast concrete block): two-storey foursquare-type houses with low hipped roofs, deep eaves, full front porches on square piers and grouped windows, set back behind lawns on a curving tree-lined street. This record uses the corner foursquare of the row.

facade.notes: Morgan Park (Duluth, 1915), US Steel's model company town: foursquares and bungalows built of the company's own concrete block, with full porches, on a curving street with grass terraces, elms and birches, lawns rising from the walk

why.note: a steel company's town built of its own cement products
a planned 1910s company suburb with curving streets (City Beautiful)
